proposed.text: A hospital horizontal exit separates a ward housing 40 non-ambulatory patients from a refuge area. Under PD 1096 Rule XII, Sec. 1206, what minimum floor area must the refuge side provide?

options.text: 12.0 sq.m — based on 0.30 sq.m per ambulatory person applied to all patient types
40.0 sq.m — based on 1.00 sq.m per person as a general refuge standard
76.0 sq.m — based on 1.90 sq.m per non-ambulatory person required by Sec. 1206
112.0 sq.m — based on 2.80 sq.m per bedridden patient for full bed clearance

proposed.rationale: Original question was already source-correct and substantive; the prior edit (source-audited-article-batch-048) was degenerate, with 1-character garbage in 3 of 4 option text fields and a nonsensical rationale. Restored the original verbatim. Original source rationale: Sec. 1206 requires 1.90 sq.m per person for non-ambulatory patients in horizontal exit refuge areas. For 40 non-ambulatory patients: 40 × 1.90 = 76.0 sq.m minimum. The ambulatory standard is 0.30 sq.m per person. Non-ambulatory patients require the larger area for wheelchairs, stretchers, and staff maneuvering.
proposed.explanation: The 0.30 / 1.90 sq.m paired values are the two horizontal exit area factors. Non-ambulatory patients (Group D Div. 2) are the primary scenario for the 1.90 figure. Confusing the two values produces severely undersized refuge areas in hospital egress design.
